text:
Maria: Heads up — since ~03:00 UTC we're seeing sporadic gRPC streaming sessions drop while going through the ALB in eu-west-1. p95 latency is normal but ~0.4-0.6% of streams get reset with 504 or upstream disconnects.

Josh: Any obvious pattern? same clients, same models, single node?

Maria: Looks workload-agnostic. Mostly long-running chat streams (30s+). Errors from client: "upstream connect error or disconnect" and occasional HTTP/2 GOAWAY on the ALB side.

Lucas: That screams timeout mismatch or conntrack/NAT ephemeral port issues. Can you paste a sample log?

Maria: pasted snippets below:
```
2026-03-18T03:12:09Z [srv] stream id=0x7fae status=13 grpc_message="upstream connect error or disconnect"
ALB: target response code 504, target: i-0abc1234, client->alb ok, alb->target reset
kernel: nf_conntrack: timeout for TCP 10.0.1.45:50432 -> 34.198.12.3:443
```

Anya: ALB default idle_timeout is 60s. If backend keepalives or HTTP/2 PING cadence is >60s ALB will tear connection with GOAWAY. Are we sending periodic PINGs from runtime?

Josh: Our runtime uses HTTP/2 without explicit PINGs; we rely on TCP keepalive. Nodes have tcp_keepalive_time=120 by default. That mismatch could cause ALB to close at 60s then client tries to use pooled stream and sees GOAWAY.

Lucas: Also check NAT gateway ephemeral port churn. If node egress IPs are SNATed, a large number of concurrent streams can exhaust ephemeral ports and conntrack entries get timed out/recycled leading to mid-stream resets.

Maria: Metric check: conntrack count spikes coincide with the incidents. nf_conntrack_max is at default on some fleets (262144). Might be borderline during bursty chat traffic.

Anya: Short-term mitigation: increase ALB idle_timeout to 300s for streaming routes, and align node tcp_keepalive_time to 30s (or enable HTTP/2 keepalive pings). Also enable ALB preserve client IP or proxy-protocol on targets if possible so we see true client source.

Josh: For NAT: consider adding more NAT gateways or use EIP per node pool so we don't hit ephemeral port reuse. Or use ENIs with 1:1 nat (where supported). Also set conntrack max higher and tune timeout for ESTABLISHED.

Maria: Reproduction steps I used:
```
# keep a long-lived bidi stream and pause sending for 70s
grpcurl -import-path proto/ -proto chat.proto -d '{ }' -plaintext your-host:443 ChatService.StreamChat
# or run a small script that opens 200 concurrent streams and idles
```

Lucas: Thanks. I'll open a config PR to bump nf_conntrack_max to 800k on eu-west nodepool and add a rollout for ALB idle_timeout for streaming ALB target group.

sre-bot: Created infra ticket INFRA-3241 (eu-west idle_timeout + conntrack tuning). link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3241

Anya: Also add an e2e test that simulates many long-lived streams (80-120s idle gaps) so we catch regressions.

Maria: Agreed. For immediate prod relief we've set ALB idle_timeout=300 on the streaming TG and scaled NAT pool. Monitoring: keep an eye on 504 rate and nf_conntrack usage. :thumbsup:

Josh: I'll follow up with a postmortem if we see any further regressions. Thanks team. :pray:
